description.narrative: Contract related to: Unpacking gendered disinformation in India - deepening understanding and exploring countermeasures - Human rights and democracy are founding values of the EU. Protecting and promoting HR&D is therefore a key priority of the EU¿s external action. It is also a precondition for sustainable development and for building more inclusive, open and resilient societies.Yet, recent data show that globally, most countries are far from having acceptable human rights and democracy track records. In this context, worsened by the COVID crisis, the EU re-affirmed its commitment to support human rights and democracy worldwide by adopting the `Action Plan on Human Rights and Democracy 2020-2024¿. The Action Plan identifies priorities and key actions, to ensure that the EU plays a greater role in promoting and defending human rights and democracy throughout its external action. The Regulation (EU) 2021/947 (Global Europe) establishes the legal basis for the human rights and democracy actions. Particularly, its annex III details the areas of intervention for human rights and democracy.The overall objective of the present action is to contribute to promote and protect human rights and fundamental freedoms, democracy and the rule of law worldwide. The action will achieve this objective by supporting and strengthening civil society organisations (CSOs), democracy activists and human-rights defenders working on critical human rights and democracy issues in non-EU countries. It may also cover, where relevant, the promotion of international humanitarian law. Consequently, it will contribute to the 5 priorities of the Multiannual Indicative programme 2021-2027 as well as the specific priorities set out for the additional funding coming from the cushion.This action will mainly be implemented by EU Delegations in-country so as to: (i) better respond to the country-specific contexts; (ii) be as close as possible to the needs of the rights holders; and (iii) promote a sense of `ownership¿ of the action among local actors. The actions financed at country level will be in line with: (i) the EU action plan for human rights and democracy; (ii) EU guidelines on human rights; and (iii) the respective Human Rights and Democracy country strategies or priorities under the EU accession process. All actions will follow a human rights based approach putting people at the centre of actions and also focusing on promoting gender equality.

comment.narrative: While there is research on misinformation and disinformation more broadly no indepth research on gendered disinformation exists in the context of India.Similarly while there are some news articles and art about gendered disinformation there are no evidencebased case studies or creation of creative content intentionally framing gendered disinformation.There are no resource guides on gendered disinformation factchecking or legal remedies available for online gender based violence and disinformation.

At least 3 thematic research studies on various issues related gendered disinformation will be developed by 2025.At least 5 case studies will provide documentary evidence of violations related to gendered disinformation and provide insight into the actors tools tactics and impacts of disinformation campaigns by 2024.At least 10 journalists and artists including writers storytellers visual artists and cartoonists will use their craft to create multimedia content that generates awareness about gendered disinformation and its impacts b y 2025.At least 1000 instances of the multimedia content including essays articles digital stories visual art and comics will be viewed online by end of 2025.At least 150 women and genderdiverse individuals will have access to the resource guide on gendered disinformation and able to better understand and counter gendered disinformation in their communities.At least 200 civil society actors including feminist and queer groups HRDs journalists lawyers and others will have access to the resource guide on factchecking.At least 200 civil society actors including feminists and queer groups journalists activists and others will have access to the resource guide on legal remedies for victims of gendered disinformation and online gender based violence and will be able to seek legal recourse if needed.
